solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Labour, upset about November GE, drown their sorrows here

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the other pieces
something upset is knocked over and jumbled, so the party name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: the party name taken as written, to be rearranged
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written: the abbreviation for a general election

explanation.surface: Labour supporters, beaten at a general election in November, go off to drink away their misery.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled party name splits in two, with the other letters slotted into the gap. A lounge bar is the more comfortable room of a British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub's lounge bar is a place where people go to drink, the classic way of drowning one's sorrows.

clue.text: Trinidadian writer turned up without notes, which is a bloomer!

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top
without means the named letters are left out

parts.note: V.S. Naipaul, the Nobel-winning novelist from Trinidad
A is a musical note, used twice

explanation.surface: A novelist arriving without banknotes would be making a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: LUAPIAN loses both of its As. A bloomer is British slang for a blunder, which the exclamation mark plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: A lupin is a garden plant grown for its tall flower spikes, so it is something that blooms.

clue.text: Highveld University timetable disheartened daughters

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university
a timetable is a plan

indicators.note: losing its heart means the word's middle goes, keeping only its ends

parts.note: the first and last letters of daughters

explanation.surface: A South African university's schedule leaves its female students glum.
explanation.walkthrough: The Highveld is the high inland plateau of South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Highveld is elevated plateau country, that is, high ground or uplands.

clue.text: Fresh wagyu, fine cuts — kilos! — fed English traitor

indicators.note: fresh suggests something made new, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: the Japanese beef, taken as written to be rearranged
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: something fed takes another piece inside it

parts.note: K for kilo, made plural
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A butcher's list: fresh Japanese beef, fine cuts, kilos of it, served to an English traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: Kilos as the plural of K is a little loose. Guy Fawkes plotted to blow up Parliament in 1605 and is burned in effigy every 5 November in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy Fawkes was a conspirator in the Gunpowder Plot against King James I, so a traitor.

clue.text: Profane abuse MPs & HoL suffered?

indicators.note: the question frames the parliamentarians as having suffered, a harm that knocks the letters into disorder

parts.note: taken as written; the ampersand adds nothing, and HoL is House of Lords

explanation.surface: Asking whether members of both Houses of Parliament endured foul-mouthed insults.
explanation.definitionFit: Profane and blasphemous both describe speech that shows disrespect for what is sacred.

clue.text: Massage parlour's closure initially upset bishop

indicators.note: the closure of a word is its end, so only its final letter is taken

parts.note: the last letter of parlour

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: the first letter of upset
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop is dismayed that his massage parlour has been shut down.
explanation.definitionFit: To massage is to knead and rub the body, and a rub is a massage.

clue.text: Pound ugly first thing in the morning, some sort of record

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the next piece

parts.note: a.m. stands for the morning

indicators.note: first thing means only the opening letter of the following word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of ugly
lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight

explanation.surface: A grim instruction to hammer someone unattractive at the start of the day, read as a description of a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First thing in the morning' reads as one phrase meaning early, but it splits: first thing of ugly, then in, then the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a long-playing record, a collection of tracks released together, so it is one kind of record.

clue.text: Old Mexican detective settled south of Arizona

indicators.note: in a down entry, south of means placed below the next piece

parts.note: AZ is the postal code for Arizona
tec is a short slang word for detective

explanation.surface: A police investigator who has made a home just below the US border state.
explanation.walkthrough: Arizona borders Mexico, which makes the geography plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aztecs were the people who ruled central Mexico before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: Odd bits of black rock that's sticky and sweet

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the noun: the thing that's sticky and sweet

indicators.note: the odd bits are the letters in odd-numbered positions of the word

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of black
lava is molten rock, which hardens into rock

explanation.surface: Fragments of dark volcanic rock described as gooey and sugary.
explanation.definitionFit: Baklava is a Middle Eastern pastry of filo layers and nuts soaked in honey syrup, so sticky and sweet.

clue.text: A new Kahlo framed by Julius's factotum

indicators.note: a picture framed by something is surrounded by it on all sides

parts.note: the setter Julius refers to himself, so his is my
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
Frida Kahlo, the Mexican painter

explanation.surface: The setter owning a newly found, framed Frida Kahlo painting.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter's own pseudonym stands for me or my.
explanation.definitionFit: Man Friday, from Robinson Crusoe's servant, means a loyal assistant who does all sorts of jobs, as a factotum does.

clue.text: Old City mate: 'your mum's outside'

parts.note: a pal is a mate, a friend

indicators.note: the mother word sits outside, wrapping around the possessive abbreviation

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mum
yr is the written abbreviation for your

explanation.surface: Someone quoting a jibe about a friend's mother being out, with an old city tacked on.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it read as playground banter; the possessive 's on mum's means 'mum is', placing her outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Palmyra is an ancient ruined city in the Syrian desert, once a rich caravan centre.

clue.text: Portend clear-out of brittle cryptocurrency

indicators.note: clearing out a word empties its interior, leaving only its two end letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of brittle
a crypto token is a unit of digital currency

explanation.surface: A warning that dumping fragile crypto holdings is a bad omen.
explanation.definitionFit: To betoken is to be a sign of something to come, which is what portend means.

clue.text: Assassin in Japan strangles assassin in Japan

indicators.note: strangling grips something tight within, so the answer is held inside the words that follow

parts.note: found across the end of assassin, the word in and the start of Japan

explanation.surface: An absurd tautology: a Japanese killer throttling another Japanese killer.
explanation.walkthrough: The repetition is the trick: the first phrase defines, and the second phrase contains the letters running across its word breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninjas were covert agents of feudal Japan, hired as spies and assassins.

clue.text: Bar firm's leader inhibiting current growth down under

indicators.note: inhibiting is read as in-hibiting, holding something inside the joined pieces

parts.note: a pub is a bar
a company's leader is its chair
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A pub company boss holding back the flow of money growth in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down under' looks like Australia but is meant literally: below the waist.
explanation.definitionFit: Pubic hair grows in the genital region, low on the body, so it is jokingly a growth found down below.

clue.text: Sweet warmed up in the style of rude boy music

parts.note: baked means heated in the oven
à la means in the style of
ska is the Jamaican music of the rude boy subculture

explanation.surface: A warmed-over pastiche of Jamaican rude boy sounds being called sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Baked Alaska is a dessert of ice cream and sponge covered in meringue and briefly baked, and a sweet is a dessert.

clue.text: Jacks' muscles

definitions.meaning: first meaning: jacks are sailors, and AB (able seaman) is a sailor, so the plural fits
second meaning: short for abdominal muscles

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe makes it read as sailors' muscles; jack tar and AB are both crossword sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Able seamen are abbreviated as ABs, and the stomach muscles are informally called abs.

clue.text: Hard-top or convertible Beetle?

indicators.note: something convertible can be changed into another form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether the classic VW Beetle is a fixed-roof car or a soft-top.
explanation.walkthrough: Beetle reads as the Volkswagen car, but the definition is the insect; the capital is only its place at the start of a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A beetle is an insect, and insects belong to the arthropods, jointed-legged invertebrates, so the definition is an example.

clue.text: After change of heart, Starmer rubbishes Dark Age philosopher

indicators.note: a change of heart rearranges the middle letters of the name, swapping their order

parts.note: Keir Starmer, the British Labour prime minister

indicators.note: rubbishing something trashes it, so the letters of the phrase are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A political jibe: the prime minister, having changed his mind, dismisses a medieval-minded thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: KEIR with its middle two letters swapped gives KIER; DARK AGE rearranged gives KEGAARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Søren Kierkegaard was a 19th-century Danish thinker, often called the father of existentialism.

clue.text: Decorated knight — boring, vulgar newspaper boss

indicators.note: boring means drilling through, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: garish means showy and vulgar
N is the chess abbreviation for knight
ed is short for editor

explanation.surface: A knighted press baron who is both dull and crude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decorated knight' looks like one phrase; Decorated is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To garnish is to adorn a dish or object, so garnished means adorned or embellished.

clue.text: Aircraft tech that tracks one crossing the Atlantic?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a radio device on a plane that answers radar signals so it can be followed
second, punning meaning: trans- means across, and the Atlantic is jokingly called the pond

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented second sense, split as trans + ponder.
explanation.definitionFit: A transponder is an aircraft unit that receives a radar signal and replies, letting air traffic control track the plane.

clue.text: Closely followed boss after cycling, showing sign of exertion

indicators.note: cycling moves letters round from the front of the word to its back

parts.note: a head is a boss
a red face shows effort

explanation.surface: A cyclist tailing the boss, flushed from the effort.
explanation.walkthrough: HEAD with its first letter moved to the end gives EADH, and once more ADHE.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere to a rule or plan is to stick to it faithfully, to follow it closely.

clue.text: Slightly potty, occasionally fiery

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of fiery

explanation.surface: A description of someone a bit mad who now and then loses their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Fey describes someone whimsical, otherworldly and a little odd, so mildly crazy in manner.

clue.text: He's found at the bow, following little fish, wasting time

parts.note: f. is the abbreviation for following

indicators.note: wasting means losing or squandering, so the letter for the time unit drops out

parts.note: a tiddler is a tiny fish
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A sailor at the front of a ship, behind a small fish, idling.
explanation.walkthrough: The bow looks like a ship's prow; it is the stick drawn across violin strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddler plays the violin, drawing a bow across the strings.

clue.text: Tries to get in authentic practice session

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: real means authentic
a judge tries a case, that is, hears it

explanation.surface: Someone attempting to get into a genuine training session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' looks like attempts; here it is the courtroom sense, a judge trying a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a run-through before a performance, a session for practising.

clue.text: Sharp article, clever

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
cute can mean shrewd or clever

explanation.surface: Praise for a newspaper piece that is witty and smart.
explanation.definitionFit: Acute means keen and perceptive, as sharp does of a mind.

clue.text: List of characters penned by Colin Dexter

indicators.note: the answer's letters are written inside, held by the author's name

parts.note: found across the end of Colin and the start of Dexter

explanation.surface: A cast list of the people in a Colin Dexter novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Colin Dexter wrote the Inspector Morse detective novels.
explanation.definitionFit: An index is an alphabetical list, for example of names and subjects at the back of a book.

clue.text: With which to copy lover boy endlessly covered in kisses?

indicators.note: covered in means wrapped by the pieces on either side

parts.note: X is the symbol for a kiss, here two of them

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is removed

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love, a boy in art

explanation.surface: A romantic young man smothered in kisses, framed as a question about copying.
explanation.walkthrough: EROS loses its last letter, and the two kisses go on either side.
explanation.definitionFit: A Xerox is a photocopier, the brand-name machine used to make copies.

clue.text: Dad runs search, having lost son in area of US theatre

indicators.note: having lost means a letter is taken away from the preceding word

parts.note: pa is an informal word for dad
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a quest is a search
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A father organising a hunt for his missing boy in an American theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: QUEST without its S gives QUET.
explanation.definitionFit: In American theatres the parquet is the ground-floor seating at the front, what Britons call the stalls.

clue.text: Tail a sports car performing a U-turn outside

indicators.note: a U-turn sends a thing back the way it came, so the letters run the other way
outside means wrapping around the other piece

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, is a sports car
taken as written

explanation.surface: Following a sports car that swings round to go back.
explanation.definitionFit: To tag along behind someone is to follow them, which is the verb sense of tail.

clue.text: Academic introducing Switzerland to green energy sector

indicators.note: introducing means bringing something inside, so one piece is put into another

parts.note: solar power is a green energy sector
CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: A researcher bringing the Swiss into the renewable power industry.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person engaged in study, the same as an academic.

clue.text: Avoid automaker

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to evade or duck out of
second meaning: the American car brand

explanation.definitionFit: To dodge is to evade, and Dodge is an American car manufacturer.

clue.text: Great photographs capturing Republican race

parts.note: grand means great

indicators.note: capturing means taking something prisoner, holding it inside

parts.note: pix is informal for pictures
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: Impressive pictures snapped of a political contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand prix is a major international motor race, such as a Formula One event.
